title: Workspaces
blurb: Nine desktops in one terminal, and a side rail that shows it all.

greet: Nine workspaces, all yours. Let us visit one.
Hi. Time to spread out a little.
finish: Nine desks and you know your way around all of them.

steps.title: Visit workspace 2
steps.note: Your two windows wait on workspace 1.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then w, then 2. The dock at the top shows where you are.

steps.title: Make it yours
steps.note: Each workspace has its own windows and layout.
steps.hint: In window mode, n opens a window here.

steps.title: Jump straight back
steps.note: alt and a number skips the prefix.
steps.hint: Hold alt (option on a Mac) and press 1. ctrl+b w 1 does the same.

web.hint: Hold alt (option on a Mac) and press 1. If the browser takes it, ctrl+b w 1 does the same.

terminal.hint: Hold alt and press 1. On a Mac, set Option as Meta in your terminal. ctrl+b w 1 does the same.

steps.title: Send a window, stay here
steps.note: ctrl+alt and a number sends the window away. You stay put.
steps.hint: Hold ctrl and alt (option on a Mac), then press 2. The window leaves, and you stay on workspace 1.

terminal.hint: Hold ctrl and alt, then press 2. On a Mac, set Option as Meta in your terminal first.

steps.title: Send a window and follow
steps.note: In the workspace menu, shift and a number moves the window, and you go with it.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, w, then shift+3, which is #.

steps.title: Open the rail
steps.note: Sessions, windows, agents and files, at a glance.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then b. The rail opens on the right.

steps.title: Walk the rail
steps.note: s steps in. j and k move, enter jumps there.
steps.hint: Press s. j twice lands on the first window, the one marked w1. Enter takes you there.

steps.title: See every workspace
steps.note: A picker with a preview of each one.
steps.hint: ctrl+b, then shift+w. Arrows pick one, enter goes there.

explainer.body: On your machine the rail lists every session, and sessions on your other machines too. ctrl+b S switches between them.
